current_definition: Optimistic, especially when facing difficulty; cheerfully confident that things will turn out well.
Having mixed or contradictory feelings about something at the same time, unable to commit to one clear position or attitude.
Using very few words; brief in speech or expression, but without any sense of rudeness or coldness.
Stubbornly refusing to obey, cooperate, or change—resisting authority or instruction even when direct pressure is applied.
Too great, beautiful, or extreme to be described in words; beyond ordinary expression.
To become less strong, severe, or intense; to gradually die down after reaching a peak.
To make a bad situation better, even if not perfect; to ease or improve conditions.
To give a false impression of something; to show that something is not what it appears to be, or to directly contradict what is claimed.
To stop someone from feeling angry or hostile, typically by making a practical gesture or giving a small concession.
To laugh at or mock someone with contempt, treating them as stupid or not worth taking seriously.
The quality of being completely honest and open in what you say, even when the truth is uncomfortable or unwelcome.
A strong and habitual liking or preference for a particular thing or activity.
A short break from something difficult, painful, or unpleasant; a brief period of relief before something hard continues.
A person or thing that represents the most perfect or concentrated example of a quality or type.
Something that stands out from the normal pattern around it; a measurable outlier that does not fit expectations.
